summary: This informational document analyzes security threats to Simplified Multicast Forwarding, including weaknesses in its duplicate packet detection and relay set selection. It does not propose solutions. It also updates RFC 7186 regarding threats to the relay set selection.

eli5.summary: Before locking a door, you look at all the ways someone could sneak in. This lists the ways attackers could trick a network that passes messages on to many devices.

questions: what is duplicate packet detection in manet
what is link spoofing in manet
subtitle: How an attacker can fool multicast forwarding in wireless mesh networks by abusing duplicate detection and relay selection.

tldr.problem: Simplified Multicast Forwarding (SMF) defines no explicit security measures, yet it runs in decentralized wireless networks where attacks are easy.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC analyzes attacks on SMF's two components, duplicate packet detection and relay set selection, covering TTL tampering, sequence number tricks, hash-assist value removal, and link and identity spoofing.
tldr.outcome: It proposes no solutions, only pointers to possible protection. It updates RFC 7186 regarding threats to relay set selection that uses NHDP.

facts.label: SMF components
facts.value: Duplicate packet detection and relay set selection

sections.title: SMF and Its Two Weak Spots
sections.content:
SMF (RFC 6621) provides basic IP multicast forwarding for wireless mesh and Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (MANETs). It has two main components: duplicate packet detection (DPD) and relay set selection (RSS). It needs neighborhood discovery from lower-layer information, a MANET routing protocol, or NHDP (RFC 6130); this document assumes NHDP is used.

The analysis assumes no IPsec or lower-layer protection, since not every MANET router can support it. An attacker is a device in the network that intentionally tries to compromise SMF routers' information bases and may generate syntactically correct SMF control messages. The RFC makes no claim of completeness and notes jamming can enhance any of the attacks.
sections.eli5: Messages in this kind of network must avoid being repeated forever, and someone must decide who passes them on. Both jobs can be tricked.

sections.title: Attacking Duplicate Packet Detection
sections.content:
Routers remember recently seen multicast packets and silently drop repeats. An attacker can pre-activate detection, so a valid packet arriving later looks like a duplicate, or deactivate it, so true duplicates are forwarded again, wasting load and battery.

Hop limit attack. Routers forward only packets with TTL greater than 1. An attacker forwards a packet with TTL cut to 1, without jitter so it arrives first. The neighbor records the packet, does not forward it, then discards the real copy (TTL 63) as a duplicate. Integrity checks usually zero the TTL when computing, so this is hard to detect.

Identification-based DPD. Packets are identified by source address plus a sequence number. In a pre-play attack the attacker injects an invalid packet with the same pair, or a predicted future one, so the valid packet is dropped. In sequence number wrangling it changes the number on forwarded packets, so duplicates look new; for n routers this causes n-1 retransmissions and a broadcast storm.

Hash-based DPD. The hash is not cryptographic, so collisions are possible; when a source sees one, it adds a Hash-Assist Value (HAV) option. An attacker who sees a HAV can strip it, making the packet look like a duplicate and be dropped.
sections.eli5: Imagine a teacher who throws away any note she has seen before. A trickster could hand her a fake note first, or scribble numbers so she thinks old notes are new.

sections.title: Attacking Relay Set Selection
sections.content:
SMF provides a framework for RSS rather than one algorithm. RFC 6621 names three: E-CDS, S-MPR and MPR-CDS. Common threats such as denial of service, eavesdropping, message timing attacks and broadcast storm are covered in RFC 7186. An attacker can degrade the system to classical flooding, or mask parts of the network from the multicast domain.

E-CDS. A router makes itself a relay if it has higher priority than all symmetric neighbors, or no path through higher-priority neighbors links the top neighbor to the others. Link spoofing, advertising nonexistent links with a high priority, makes the attacker a "super" relay and keeps legitimate routers from relaying. Identity spoofing lets the attacker declare a spoofed router's priority higher, which stops others relaying, or lower, which forces others to relay and degrades forwarding to flooding.

S-MPR is disrupted by link and identity spoofing because it depends on declared willingness and connectivity. MPR-CDS combines E-CDS and S-MPR and inherits both sets of weaknesses.
sections.eli5: The network picks a few helpers to pass messages along. A liar can claim to be everyone's best friend, or pretend to be someone else, to make the picking go wrong.

sections.title: Possible Protection and Its Limits
sections.content:
The RFC specifies no mechanism, but suggests directions. For identification-based detection, random sequence numbers avoid some pre-activation attacks, and timestamps help if numbers must be predictable. For hash-based detection, cryptographically strong hashes make collisions effectively impossible and remove the need for a HAV.

RFC 7182 defines integrity check values and timestamps, and RFC 7183 uses them to protect NHDP with shared keys. Implementing it is advisable if SMF uses NHDP, and helps against identity spoofing in HELLO messages. It does not stop attackers who can generate valid ICVs. With asymmetric keys (RFC 7859), key revocation becomes part of the challenge.

Since RFC 7183 does not protect multicast data packets and SMF specifies no way to do so, duplicate packet detection stays vulnerable. Even datagram-level integrity would not stop TTL attacks, because mutable fields are generally excluded from ICV calculation.
sections.eli5: Signing messages helps catch fakers, but not if the faker has a real signature, and the number of hops left on a message can still be changed.
